absent: Encoding of shadow page role union and permission bit constants.
Logic of hugepage attribute query and mixed marker set clear helpers.
Numeric values of hugepage level bounds and page size constants.
Memory slot lookup, iteration and address space count helpers.
Notifier node layout and detailed write callback obligations.
MMU specific write tracking performed alongside external notifiers.

findings.text: Post update routine refreshes hugepage mixed tracking after guest memory attributes change. It first confirms private memory support is present, otherwise signals a warning condition and declines further work. On success it walks hugepage levels in increasing order so higher levels observe lower level decisions, adjusting per slot mixed markers for partially overlapped edges by probing current attributes and clearing markers for fully enclosed units, while skipping edge units that fall outside slot bounds or cannot form a hugepage due to misalignment. The routine always reports no additional rescan is required.

Caller must already hold the MMU lock in write mode together with the slots lock when entering the attribute post update path. The implementation asserts both holdings on entry and assumes slot descriptors remain stable throughout the scan.

Hugepage attribute reconciliation proceeds strictly from smaller to larger sizes. Edge units that straddle the changed interval are evaluated individually against current attributes to set or clear a mixed marker, fully covered units have their marker cleared unconditionally because only new attributes can remain, and trailing partial units receive the same edge evaluation when contained in the slot.

Shadow and TDP page descriptor anchors linkage for active lists and hash lookup, distinguishes TDP versus legacy shadowing plus synchronization and validity generation, records role and guest frame identity with a pointer to the shadow entries and cached translation results, counts active root usage with separate handling for TDP reference counting, flags host MMIO mappings and NX hugepage restrictions, tracks unsynchronized children or an external table pointer for confidential guests, links to parent entries either through reverse mapping heads or direct TDP parent pointers, maintains a child unsync bitmap and a candidate list for NX huge page promotion, with architecture specific reclamation state. TDP entry pointers are RCU annotated references to sixty four bit entries.

Fault context bundles immutable inputs describing fault address, error encoding and prefetch hint, plus decoded permission and privilege flags, global mode flags for TDP operation, private mapping and NX hugepage mitigation, a mutable disallow flag for large mappings, a three stage level negotiation from maximum through host constrained to final goal, the translated frame number without alias selection bits and its containing slot pointer, fault in outputs covering sequence, frame, reference counted page and writability, and a marker for writes that modify their own translation tables.

Fault resolution uses seven named results. RET_PF_CONTINUE means proceed, RET_PF_RETRY means attempt again, RET_PF_EMULATE means software emulation is required, RET_PF_WRITE_PROTECTED means copy on write handling, RET_PF_INVALID means invalid access, RET_PF_FIXED means already resolved, RET_PF_SPURIOUS means no action needed.

Base address masking spans low twelve through fifty one. Level shift is derived from page shift plus per level stride times depth minus one. Index extraction shifts by that amount and masks to bits per level. Per level address and offset masks combine the base mask with low bit clearing or isolation for the level reach. Entries per table equal two raised to bits per level.
Invalid PAE root sentinel is defined as numeric zero.

Root frame masking returns zero for mirrored shadow roots used for confidential guests, otherwise it returns the direct mapping bits configured for the virtual machine. Mirrored roots therefore need no alias adjustment while shared roots do.

Memory management tracing uses subsystem kvmmmu with include path mmu and include file mmutrace. Recorded page attributes include validity generation, guest frame number, role encoding, root usage count and synchronization state, with formatted output rendering level, entry width, quadrant, directness, access rights, validity, execute and dirty tracking flags.
Fault error decoding maps present, write, user, protection key, shadow stack, SGX, reserved bit and fetch conditions to short mnemonics P, W, U, PK, SS, SGX, RSVD and F respectively.
Notifier subsystem initialization prepares an empty listener list and initializes its sleepable read copy update control. It reports success unconditionally in the examined path.

Enabling external write tracking is rejected for confidential TDX guests. Otherwise acquisition of the architecture slots mutex serializes first use, redundant enablement is skipped when any tracking is already active, per slot tracking storage is allocated for every address space slot with partial allocations intentionally retained on failure for later cleanup or retry, and the enabled flag is published with release ordering only after all storage is visible.

Listener registration validates a non null handle owned by the current process, lazily enables external tracking when not yet active and propagates enablement failures, acquires a reference on the virtual machine, then inserts the node at the head of the notifier list under exclusive MMU lock protection.
Listener removal deletes the node under exclusive MMU lock, waits for outstanding sleepable read side traversals to drain, then releases the virtual machine reference.

Write notification iterates registered listeners only when the list is non empty. Traversal holds a sleepable read lock and invokes each installed write callback with address, new bytes and length plus the listener context.

Per frame write tracking add and remove both resolve the containing slot under sleepable read protection and fail when no slot covers the frame. On success they mutate tracking state under exclusive MMU lock and then drop the read protection before reporting success.

Page tracking uses the architecture slots mutex to serialize enablement, the MMU lock in write mode to mutate listener membership and per frame tracking, and sleepable read protection for slot lookup and callback iteration, with removal synchronizing to guarantee no callback remains in flight before reference release.

When page tracking support is compiled out, initialization reports success without action and write notification is a no operation, while the combined per vcpu helper forwards to the notifier path and then to MMU specific write tracking.

Paging templates provide three configurations. Sixty four bit paging and extended page tables use eight byte entries with nine bits per level, while thirty two bit paging uses four byte entries with ten bits per level. Each variant selects its own walker type and name prefix, with accessed and dirty handling always available except for extended tables where availability depends on the address disable control.

Maximum fully walked levels are deep for sixty four bit and extended configurations but limited to two for legacy thirty two bit handling. Thirty six bit page size extension directory geometry uses a four bit field starting at bit thirteen with a mask derived from that width and position.

Guest walk state records current and maximum levels, per level table frame numbers, cached entries and prefetch entries, physical addresses of entries, user pointers to entries, per level writability and access rights, accumulated entry access, final translated frame and a fault record for failures.

Guest entry interpretation distinguishes legacy presence based on a single present flag from extended table presence based on any of low three permission bits plus an optional supervisor mode execution protection bit. Access rights are translated from extended read write execute controls including user execute, or from legacy present write user and execute disable controls. Clean entries lose write permission unless dirty tracking is unsupported or the dirty flag is set. Prefetch drops invalid, unaccessed or reserved entries. Accessed and dirty maintenance sets flags with tracing, consults nested logging for extended tables on dirty transitions, and skips updates for read only slots.

Attempting external write tracking on TDX virtual machines fails as unsupported. Allocation failure during enablement leaves already allocated per slot metadata in place rather than rolling back, relying on slot teardown for reclamation and allowing user retry without loss.
Virtual machine reference acquisition increments the user count to pin the instance across notifier lifetime and similar long lived uses.

Derived paging helpers adapt the generic base mask to the template entry width, provide per level address and offset masks plus index computation using template stride, define guest dirty and accessed masks from template shifts, and convert entries to frame numbers at a given level with a four kilobyte default.
Thirty six bit extension handling extracts a small high bit field from directory entries and shifts it into guest frame number space to account for address bits beyond thirty two.
Internal headers use conventional include guards and the page track source defines a module prefixed log format.
